title: encrypted drives are not checked for SMART data
line: Disks encrypted or formatted as a whole, without a partition table, are now checked for SMART problems and shown in Info Center.
explanation: The SMART monitor only treated storage volumes whose usage is a partition table as real disks, to avoid running smartctl on partitions. A disk encrypted with LUKS as a whole (or otherwise used without a partition table) reports usage Encrypted/FileSystem, so it was skipped as 'bad type' and never checked. The change also accepts such volumes when their parent is a hard-disk drive and the volume isn't a partition (no UDisks 'Table' property).

commits.message:
kded: also check disks that have no partition table

Only volumes holding a partition table were treated as devices, so a
disk encrypted or formatted as a whole was skipped and never checked
for SMART data. Also accept such volumes when they aren't partitions.

BUG: 499924

media.caption: Master: whole-disk LUKS sdd is skipped as 'bad type Encrypted', only sda is checked
With the fix: sdd is evaluated and smartctl is requested for /dev/sdd; the LUKS partition sda1 is still skipped
